review_candidates.description: What We Do Since 1863, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has worked to preserve human dignity and relieve suffering caused by war and armed violence. We engage with authorities and armed forces on all sides, often confidentially, pressing for access to detainees to improve their living conditions and urging compliance with international humanitarian law to protect non-combatants, including from digital threats. Purpose The Prehospital Emergency Care Field Officer (PHEC FO) manages First & Aid & Prehospital Emergency Care (FAPHEC) programmes and resources in Somalia, ensuring effective implementation, monitoring, reporting and follow-up against approved objectives and resources. The role holder supports the development of safe, effective and context-appropriate first aid and prehospital emergency care systems, ensuring that wounded and sick people receive timely care and are appropriately referred for further treatment. The role also strengthens the emergency preparedness and response capacity of health systems and relevant actors to manage prehospital emergencies and mass-casualty incidents. The PHEC FO provides technical leadership for FAPHEC activities, ensuring effective planning, coordination, resource management and alignment with ICRC priorities and delegation objectives. This is a national/resident position based in Mogadishu, Somalia. Accountabilities & Functional Responsibilities Develops and maintains an overall understanding of the FAPHEC system, including needs, capacities, resources, local coping mechanisms and referral pathways, and identifies the appropriate role and added value of the ICRC and Movement partners Develops and strengthens local FAPHEC capacities by designing, implementing and adapting context-appropriate projects and Plans of Action with relevant stakeholders, aligned with ICRC guidance and organizational priorities Builds and strengthen the capacity of FAPHEC stakeholders, ICRC and non-ICRC personnel, through coaching, technical support and contextualized ICRC guidance and educational materials, promoting competent, safe, principled and locally adapted emergency response Develops constructive partnerships and coordination mechanisms among relevant FAPHEC stakeholders, including relevant Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners, to strengthen preparedness, response capacity and sustainable local ownership Integrates security-management approaches, including the Safer Access Framework and Health Care in Danger, into FAPHEC preparedness and response, and supports stakeholders to anticipate and manage emergencies safely Develops and delivers FAPHEC training programmes for first responders and healthcare staff, covering trauma care, patient assessment, stabilization, referral and mass casualty management Delivers and facilitates FAPHEC courses, including Basic Emergency Care, First Responder Trauma Course, Clinical Training of Trainers (ToT) adapted to the needs and level of the target group Promotes systematic patient assessment, effective teamwork, clinical decision-making and evidence-based prehospital emergency care practices Supports health authorities, National Societies and healthcare facilities to strengthen emergency preparedness and response capacities, based on context-specific risks, needs and available resources Accountabilities & Functional Responsibilities Supports the development and implementation of SOPs, preparedness and response plans, clinical pathways and referral mechanisms for emergencies and mass casualty and uses monitoring tools and indicators (e.g. MAD) to assess FAPHEC activities against agreed objectives Analyzes programme data, training results and field observations to identify gaps and areas prehospital emergency care training/education and prehospital emergency care programming Postgraduate diploma/certificate in public health or emergency/disaster medicine and mass casualty management dispatch/communication and humanitarian project management Desired Profile And Skills 5 years professional experience in similar health activities Trauma and prehospital care knowledge Strong economic and cultural aspects in Somalia Fluency in written and spoken English and Somali language Proficiency in MS Office suite Flexibility and willingness to travel within Somalia Language English review_candidates.title: Merchandiser -1872
review_candidates.description: To ensure the proper merchandising, availability, visibility, and presentation of frozen food products across assigned retail outlets in accordance with the approved visit schedule, merchandising standards, and planograms. The In-Store Merchandiser is responsible for maintaining optimal shelf availability, applying the First In, First Out (FIFO) principle, monitoring product expiry dates, ensuring correct product rotation, and identifying replenishment needs. The role also involves monitoring stock and display conditions, reporting operational issues and sales opportunities to the Sales Team, and coordinating with relevant stakeholders to maintain product quality, maximizing shelf presence, and support sales growth. Responsibilities: Outlet Visits and Schedule Compliance Visit assigned outlets according to the approved schedule, maintain a regular presence, and complete all planned merchandising activities on time. Record completed visits and report missed visits or access issues to the direct supervisor. Merchandising, Visibility and Shelf Arrangement Arrange and display frozen products according to approved planograms, shelf layouts, and outlet requirements, in the designated freezer sections. Keep products organized, clearly visible, and appealing, with labels and packaging facing customers and correct positioning, facings, and shelf allocation. Monitor brand and product visibility against approved merchandising guidelines, and identify opportunities to improve shelf positioning, facings, and displays within agreed requirements. Report unauthorized product relocations, missing displays, reduced shelf space, or deviations from planograms. Support approved promotions, special displays, and in-store campaigns. Stock Replenishment and Availability Monitor shelf stock levels and replenish from backroom or freezer stock when required and permitted by outlet procedures, placing products correctly and keeping shelves stocked throughout the visit. Identify out-of-stock and low-stock items, report replenishment needs to the Sales Team, and highlight recurring shortages or assortment gaps across assigned outlets. Stock Rotation and Expiry Management Apply FIFO consistently, check expiry dates during every visit, and rotate products appropriately. review_candidates.title: Marine ERP Executive - MariApps / PMS
review_candidates.description: About the Role We are implementing MariApps ERP across our fleet and are looking for a Marine ERP Executive to support the implementation, standardization, and continued development of the system across our vessels and shore organization. This is not a conventional IT support position. We are looking for someone who understands both sides of the requirement: Marine: vessel machinery, equipment, planned maintenance, spares, technical documentation, certification, Class/Flag/statutory requirements, and actual onboard working practices. ERP: MariApps/PMS functionality, master data, equipment hierarchy, maintenance jobs, workflows, testing, troubleshooting, implementation, and user support. The successful candidate will act as the technical and functional link between our vessels, shore-based teams, and the MariApps ERP provider, ensuring that operational and regulatory requirements are correctly translated into the ERP system. Key Responsibilities 1. MariApps ERP Implementation & Support Support implementation and rollout of MariApps ERP across the fleet. Work closely with vessel teams, Technical Superintendents, Operations, Procurement, and other shore departments. Act as a key interface between the organization and ERP provider. Translate practical vessel requirements into clear ERP functional requirements. Coordinate system configuration, testing, implementation, and improvements. Develop and execute realistic test scenarios for marine ERP/PMS workflows. Identify system bugs, configuration issues, and process gaps. Coordinate corrective actions with the ERP provider and verify solutions through retesting. Maintain and follow up ERP issues, enhancement requests, and system improvements through closure. Support migration, validation, and standardization of ERP master data. 2. Planned Maintenance System Develop, review, and improve vessel machinery/equipment registers and PMS structures. Establish appropriate equipment hierarchy and parent-child relationships. Review equipment maintenance requirements against: OEM manuals and recommendations Classification Society requirements Flag State requirements Statutory requirements International marine regulations Company maintenance standards Vessel-specific operational requirements Review calendar-based, running-hour-based, condition-based, and statutory maintenance routines. Ensure critical equipment and associated maintenance requirements are appropriately identified and configured. Support management of overdue maintenance, deferred jobs, breakdown maintenance, and maintenance history. 3. Machinery & Equipment Knowledge The candidate should have sound practical understanding of shipboard machinery and systems, including: Main and auxiliary engines Propulsion systems Generators and electrical machinery Steering gear Pumps, compressors, and purifiers Fuel, lubricating oil, cooling water, and compressed-air systems Hydraulic systems Deck machinery, winches, and cranes Firefighting and lifesaving equipment Pollution-prevention equipment Relevant navigation and communication equipment interfaces Critical equipment and machinery supporting DP operations, where applicable Experience with offshore vessels would be an advantage. 4. Class, Flag & Regulatory Compliance The candidate should understand how vessel maintenance, inspections, testing, certification, and documentation relate to: Classification Society requirements Flag State requirements SOLAS MARPOL ISM Code IMO requirements statutory surveys and certification annual, intermediate, special, and renewal survey regimes periodic testing and inspection requirements The individual should be capable of ensuring these requirements are appropriately represented within vessel ERP/PMS workflows where applicable. 5. Technical Documentation & Master Data Review and standardize machinery/equipment naming and coding conventions. Validate equipment technical particulars. Develop and maintain equipment hierarchy. Link equipment with maintenance routines, spares, manuals, drawings, certificates, and other supporting documents. Ensure vessel technical documentation is correctly structured within the ERP system. Support spare-parts identification and equipment/spares linkage. Assist in establishing critical spare requirements and appropriate stock levels. Monitor and improve ERP master-data quality across the fleet. 6. Vessel & Shore User Support Support Masters, Chief Engineers, Second Engineers, and vessel personnel in effective use of MariApps. Assist Technical Superintendents and other shore users with ERP/PMS functionality. Investigate problems raised by vessels and determine whether they arise from: system functionality, system configuration, master data, incorrect workflow, or user practices. Provide practical training and guidance to vessel and shore personnel. Develop user guides, standard procedures, and good practices for using the ERP/PMS. Promote consistent ERP usage and data quality across the fleet. The successful candidate must be able to convert: Vessel technical requirement → Maintenance / compliance requirement → MariApps configuration → Testing → Implementation → Vessel feedback → Closure Candidate Profile Essential Degree/Diploma in Marine Engineering or equivalent marine technical qualification. Sailing experience in the engine department. Strong practical understanding of vessel machinery and maintenance. Good working knowledge of marine Planned Maintenance Systems. Practical experience using marine ERP/PMS applications. Understanding of machinery maintenance schedules, equipment hierarchy, maintenance history, spares, and technical documentation. Familiarity with Class, Flag, statutory, and international regulatory requirements. Ability to work effectively with marine personnel as well as ERP/software teams. Strong troubleshooting, documentation, communication, and coordination skills. Ability to independently understand a vessel-side problem and convert it into a clear ERP requirement. Strongly Preferred Hands-on experience with MariApps ERP/PMS. Marine Engineer with Second Engineer or Chief Engineer sailing experience. Experience developing or maintaining PMS master data rather than only using PMS for job completion. Previous shore-based experience in fleet technical management, ERP/PMS implementation, or marine technical support. Experience participating in an ERP implementation, data migration, system rollout, or major PMS improvement project. Experience with offshore vessels, particularly DP2 AHTS, would be advantageous. What We Are Specifically Looking For We are not looking for a generic IT support or software engineer who happens to have worked with an ERP system. The ideal candidate is a marine engineer who understands how machinery is actually maintained onboard and who can convert that knowledge into an effective MariApps/PMS structure. Ideal Candidate You may be a particularly strong fit if you can confidently answer yes to most of these questions: Have you sailed as a Marine Engineer? Can you understand an engine-room machinery manual and convert OEM maintenance recommendations into PMS jobs? Do you understand running-hour, calendar, condition-based, and statutory maintenance? Can you build or review an equipment hierarchy? Do you understand critical equipment and critical spares? Have you worked hands-on with MariApps? Have you created, corrected, or maintained PMS master data? Do you understand the relationship between machinery maintenance, Class/Flag/statutory requirements, surveys, and certification? Can you work directly with an ERP provider to explain a marine requirement, test their solution, and confirm whether it works in practice? Can you train vessel personnel to use an ERP/PMS correctly? Why This Role Matters ERP implementation in a marine organization is not simply a software project. The quality of the system ultimately depends on the quality of the marine technical information, maintenance philosophy, master data, workflows, and user practices behind it. This position will therefore play an important role in ensuring that MariApps becomes a practical fleet-management tool rather than simply a system for recording transactions. The individual will have significant interaction with vessels, Technical Superintendents, management, and the ERP provider and will help establish the long-term standard for ERP/PMS usage across the fleet. Application Requirements Interested candidates should submit an updated CV clearly indicating: Marine Engineering qualification and Certificate of Competency, if applicable. Total sea-going experience. Highest rank sailed. Vessel types worked on. ERP/PMS systems used. Specific MariApps experience, including modules used. Experience with PMS master-data creation or modification. Experience with ERP implementation, migration, testing, or rollout. Shore-based marine/technical experience, if any. Current location and availability. Candidates with demonstrated hands-on MariApps experience combined with sailing experience will be given preference.
